## 

```{bash}
# you should be able to demosntrate proficiency in working with 
cd
pwd
mkdir demo
cd demo
echo "hello" > test.txt
cp -v test.txt test_new.txt
mv test_new.txt renamed.txt
ls -lh
cat test.txt
head -n 5 test.txt
tail -n 5 test.txt
rm -i renamed.txt

```

```         
a unix command interface looks like this

command input output
```

```{bash}

passsword

```         
```         
the ssh command allows you to log in the cypress securely 
it requires password
please note that password wont show for security purposes
```

```{bash}

whoami
hostname
pwd
ls
cd 
mkdir
rm 
rm -r
```

```         
whoami - identifies the user
hostname - identifies the host - where are you working
pwd - print working directory - and shows where you are currently
ls - list the objects in the working drectory
```

```{bash}

cd ~ 
mkdir day1
mkdir data
mkdir results

```

```         
lets check what we have created
we should have day1, data, and results folder in our home directory
can we do this until here? 
```

```{bash}
echo "sample_id, phenotype, genotype" > test.txt
echo "sample_id2, phenotype, genotype" >> test.txt
echo " Hi, my_name, is, Kam" >> test.txt
head test.txt
cat test.txt

```

```         
> vs >>
> replaces the file 
>> appends the file you already have 
```

```{bash}
echo "alpha" > alpha.txt
echo "beta" > beta.txt
echo "gamma" > gamma.txt
ls
```

```         
what do you see in the environment 
how many files do you have ?
```

```{bash}
cp test.txt test_new.txt
ls
cat test_new.txt

cp -v test.txt test_verbose.txt
```

```         
-v verbose is a progress bar 
```

```{bash}
mkdir results
cd results
mv test_new.txt results
ls
ls results

```

```{bash}

ls       #list names
ls -l    #long listing
ls -lh   #long listing with human-readable sizes
ls -a    #include hidden files
ls -lt   #newest modified files first
ls -lS   #largest files first; capital S matters

```

```{bash}
# create wild card
*.txt    names ending in .txt
*t       names ending in t
t*g      names starting with t and ending with g
T*       names starting with uppercase T
t*       names starting with lowercase t

```

```{bash}
# some basic command lines 
cat long_file.txt
less long_file.txt
head long_file.txt
tail long_file.txt
head -n 5 long_file.txt
tail -n 5 long_file.txt

```

```{bash}
rm -i beta.txt

```
